title: LLM Agents as Static Level-k Players in Behavioural Games
abstract: arXiv:2606.27845v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as stand-ins in behavioural games. These stand-ins rely on the assumption that the LLM's distribution of choices meaningfully matches how humans play the same game. This study tests that assumption through two games. The first is a p-beauty contest, and the second one is a public goods game. The study first investigates five local-model settings within the same model family. These settings are varied together in a 360-cell factorial, which balances temperature, scale (0.5-32B), quantisation, instruct vs base, and framing. Each cell's distribution is then compared against whole choice distributions in published human data. Each deployment setting, except for quantisation, governs a different aspect of fidelity. Mechanically, while the dispersion of human players can be somewhat recovered through deployment settings, the strategic process behind it cannot. Through the lens of the level

translated_title: 大语言模型智能体作为行为博弈中的静态k级玩家
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用作行为博弈中的人类替代参与者，这些替代依赖于一个假设：LLM的选择分布在有意义的程度上匹配人类玩同一博弈的方式。本研究通过两个博弈检验了这一假设：一个是p Beauty Contest，另一个是公共品博弈。研究首先在同一模型家族内考察了五种本地模型设置，这些设置在一个360单元的因子设计中共同变化，涵盖温度、规模（0.5-32B）、量化、指令微调与基础模型以及提示框架。随后将每个单元的选择分布与已发表人类数据中的完整选择分布进行比较。结果表明，除量化外，每个部署设置都控制着保真度的不同方面。从机制上看，虽然人类玩家的选择分散性可以通过部署设置在一定程度上得到恢复，但其背后的策略过程却无法重现。通过k级推理的视角……
tldr: 本研究通过p Beauty Contest和公共品博弈的360单元因子实验发现，大语言模型的选择分布虽可通过部署设置部分拟合人类玩家的分散性，但其背后的策略推理过程无法被再现，表明LLM作为人类博弈行为的替代者存在根本局限。
en_tdlr: This study shows that while LLM choice distributions in behavioural games can partially match human dispersion through deployment settings, the underlying strategic reasoning process cannot be reproduced, revealing fundamental limitations of LLMs as stand-ins for human players.
